dedupe_keys.name: measurement characterization of hurricane wind loads on structures using a wireless sensing networking system

description: Measurement & Characterization of Hurricane Wind Loads on Structures Using a Wireless Sensing Networking System is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Jean-Paul Pinelli, Florida Institute of Technology (fit.edu). The researchers from Florida Institute of Technology deployed their wireless sensor network (WSN) system on the rooftop of a house near Satellite Beach, Melbourne, Florida (longitude and latitude: 28.175944, -80.592710) during the recent hurricanes Matthew and Irma passage to collect real-time data. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/DS2JT3Q. Keywords: Field deployment, measurements, wireless sensors network, hurricanes, wind pressure, wind speed. Published 2018-05-17. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated in the DesignSafe listing (publication licences offered are CC BY 4.0, ODC-By, CC0 and GPL; project page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
